configs.description: EX2200-24T-4G - 24 10/100/1000 ports without PoE and four SFP uplinks, built-in AC supply and two built-in fans, side-to-rear airflow (Table 3).
configs.name: ac

configs.description: EX2200-24T-4G-DC - the same front with a built-in DC supply (Table 3, Table 13, Figure 48): a block of four terminals (B-, A-, B+, A+) replaces the AC inlet on the rear. The guide gives the same weight (2.7 kg) and says a DC-powered switch provides no PoE, as this model has none.
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: Table 31 lists the supplied two-post mounting brackets (EX2200: provided) and a separately orderable four-post rack-mount kit with 2-inch recess front brackets, and gives no part number for the kit; no figure measures a bracket position, so no ear position is stated and no kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: The four-post rack-mount kit's part number and a dimensioned drawing of the bracket positions.

gaps.note: Searched for an end-of-life notice: only third-party lifecycle trackers answered (an end-of-sale in 2019 is reported); Juniper's own bulletin was not found, so no lifecycle is written.
gaps.wanted: Juniper's end-of-life bulletin for the EX2200 line.

gaps.note: No photograph of any EX2200 is held and the maker's image library no longer carries one; the faces are read from the guide's figures alone, which are line drawings, so colour, finish, the printing on the front (model name, logo, port numerals) and the legends on the rear are not confirmed, and the DC rear has no flat figure at all.
gaps.wanted: Straight-on studio photographs of the EX2200-24T front, its AC rear and its DC rear.

gaps.note: The four-terminal DC block of the -DC part number is chassis art; no library component has four poles and no document held gives its part, its pole pitch or its legend.
gaps.wanted: The DC terminal block's dimensions and printed legend.

gaps.note: The jack lamps carry the component's link and activity vocabulary; the guide's Status lamp switches meaning with the mode button and no per-lamp state list fits the component.
gaps.wanted: none beyond the component's own vocabulary.

airflow.note: the cooling system provides side-to-rear chassis cooling (Figure 14 for models without PoE): air enters by the side vents and leaves by the rear openings. The chassis enum has no side-to-rear value, so the side value is carried.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Hardware guide, Power Supply in EX2200 Switches: "The power supply in EX2200 switches is built in along the rear panel of the chassis", with an AC power cord inlet or DC power terminals on it; Table 4 lists "Built-in power supply" and the cooling system is two fans along the rear. Nothing in the guide describes removing or replacing either. They are part of the chassis, not bays and not components.

chassis.note: Table 5: height 1.75 in (4.45 cm), width 17.5 in (44.5 cm) and 19 in (48.2 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 10.5 in (26.7 cm), weight 6 lb (2.7 kg) for the EX2200-24T and the EX2200-24T-DC. 445.0 x 44.45 x 267.0 is carried: width and depth as the printed metric, the height as the 1U pitch Table 31 gives (1.75 in). The figures draw no ears, and the jack pitch closing on the registry at that width says the figure is the body.

colour.note: borrowed - the chassis #919599 and the jack shells #b1b2b5 are the EX2300 front photograph's medians. The guide's figures are line drawings with no colour and no EX2200 photograph is held, so these are a relative's and not a reading of this device.

front-layout.note: estimated - read off Figure 2 as described under gate-1. The 24 jacks stand in two shells of six columns at 187.3 and 277.4 mm, the first jack at 190.6 mm, the jack pitch the registry's 13.97 and a 6.27 gutter (shell step 90.1 mm), the shell boxes 89.0 mm wide, rows 14.85 mm apart, the upper row turned 180 so its lamp tabs are above as the figure shows. The four uplink cages abut on the registry's 14.25 pitch from 366.1 mm and stand 27.4 mm down. The left half of the face is blank in the figure. A long recessed slot runs along the top edge from 7.1 to 438.1 mm; it carries no printing. The guide's figure draws four small oval marks along the top edge, no vents, no model name and no logo on the front, so none is drawn and no logo zone is reserved: the real unit's printing is not known from any source held. The chassis and shell colours are borrowed from the EX2300 photographs (see colour).

gate-1.note: Figure 2 was rendered at 600 dpi and measured with a pixel ruler, together with Figure 1 whose front face it shares. The 48-port figure's front face is 2430 px across and 237 px down: 5.467 px per mm across from the 445 mm of Table 5 and 5.34 down from 44.45 mm, a 2.4 percent aspect error, so x and y are each taken from their own dimension and every position is estimated and good to about a millimetre. The jack width reads 12.7 mm, the registry's 12.7 for the ganged RJ-45 cell, on a quantity the scale never saw. The figures are perspective views from above and the front face is the near rectangle; Figure 5 (rear) is a flat elevation, 2722 px across and 266 down: 6.124 px per mm across and 5.99 down, a 2.2 percent aspect error. Figure 2's two shells stand where the last two of Figure 1 do (186.8 mm measured, 187.3 drawn).

lamps.note: Hardware guide, Tables 6 to 10 and Figures 7, 11 and 12. Each RJ-45 port and uplink has two lamps, Link/Activity and Status; Figure 11 puts them on the two tabs of the jack. The Status lamp reads out whichever of speed (SPD), duplex (DX), administrative status (EN) and PoE (POE) the Factory Reset/Mode button has selected, shown by which port-mode lamp is lit; the guide lists four port-mode lamps on every non-compact model, PoE or not. SYS is green and ALM unlit, amber or red. The jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary because a block cannot override it per lamp. Figure 12 draws the uplink lamps as two circles either side of each numeral; the left is taken as Link/Activity and the right as Status, which no figure confirms, so it is estimated. The SYS and ALM lamps are drawn as the figure draws them, oblong, and their legends tilted in the figure are printed level here.

port-numbering.note: drawing - Figure 2 prints each column's two numbers above its shell, the even number up and left of a short divider and the odd number down and right (0 and 1, 2 and 3, ... 22 and 23), and the four uplinks 0 to 3 between their two lamps. Both numbers of a column are printed above the upper jack, so which jack takes which is by analogy with the EX2300 faceplate (the upper jack takes the even number), estimated. The even numeral is drawn 2.55 mm left of its jack's centre and the odd one on its centre, as measured on Figure 1; the small divider lines between them are not drawn. Port numbers are as printed, from 0. The Junos interface names are not printed: Table 4 gives PIC 0 as 24x10/100/1000BASE-T and PIC 1 as 4x GE SFP, i.e. ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/23 and ge-0/1/0 to ge-0/1/3; they are recorded here and not in an interfaces block because the faceplate does not print them.

power.note: Table 11: maximum power consumed 50 W for the EX2200-24T and for the EX2200-24T-DC, no PoE, 170.5 BTU/hour; Table 12: AC input 100 through 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 1.8 A at 100 VAC and 0.5 A at 230 VAC for switches with no PoE ports; Table 13: DC input 36 through 75 VDC, 3.5 A maximum, power supply output 100 W, output holdup time 1 ms minimum (the guide recommends 3.5 A at 48 VDC and a 10 A breaker; its DC wiring text asks for a source of at least 7.5 A at -48 VDC, which is a facility figure and is not carried).

rear-dc.note: estimated - no flat figure of the DC rear exists in the guide: Figure 48 is a close view of the terminals and Figure 5 is the AC rear, whose inlet the guide says is replaced by "DC power terminals" ("AC power cord inlet or DC power terminals"). The DC rear is Figure 5's with the inlet replaced by a block of four terminals labelled, left to right, B-, A-, B+ and A+ (Figure 48) under a clear plastic cover, centred on the inlet's centre (419.2 mm) and drawn 36.0 x 18.4 mm; the size has no scale anchor and is estimated. The block is chassis art and not a component: the library has no four-pole DC terminal block (common/dc-terminal-24 has three poles) and the DCIM export has no row for such a part. A and B are two inputs of one supply; the guide says a DC-powered switch provides no PoE.

rear-layout.note: estimated - positions read off Figure 5 (labelled EX2200-24-4G) as described under gate-1: the management jack with the USB port under it in one housing, the RJ-45 console port, the RPS port (a rounded plate with a slotted opening and four screws), the two-hole earthing plate with the earth symbol, the ESD point, three round exhaust openings, the two small slots at 270 mm and the AC inlet, which the guide names in that order. The three openings are drawn at 142.0, 192.2 and 236.9 mm; their uneven spacing is the figure's. The guide says the two left openings have fans and the third has none and is closed on non-PoE models, so the third is drawn sealed here. The serial number ID label is a paper label carrying a real serial number and is not drawn; the power cord retainer clips are accessories and are not drawn. Figure 5 prints no legend near the inlet, so none is drawn. The jack housing is one dark recess behind the management and USB ports.

rps-port.note: estimated - the RPS port (Figure 5 callout, guide list of rear panel components) is drawn as chassis art: the plate and its opening at 50.1 to 118.0 mm and four screws. It is not a component: the library has no RPS connector and its DCIM export has no row for one. The guide names no RPS part number and no document of the RPS is held.

sources.note: EX2200 and EX2200-C Switches Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2022-02-02 (268 pages), the copy held in Juniper's EX documentation archive (https://www.juniper.net/documentation/en_US/release-independent/downloads/ex-series/ex-series-doc-archives.zip, member ex-series-doc-archives/ex2200.pdf): Figure 2 (24-port front), Figure 5 (rear), Figure 48 (DC terminals), Table 3 (models), Table 5 (chassis size and weight), Tables 6 to 10 (LEDs), the cooling system section with Figures 14 and 15, Tables 11 to 13 (power) and Table 16 (environment). The guide is the only source held for the EX2200: Juniper's datasheet is dehosted, and the maker's image library and the held photograph set have no EX2200 photograph. The guide carries Juniper's copyright and reserves its rights, so its figures were read for what is on each face and where, and none was copied; every skin here is drawn from those measurements.

uplinks.note: drawing - one row of four built-in SFP cages numbered 0 to 3 (Figure 2); the guide gives 1-gigabit SFP transceivers for fibre and copper and says an SFP uplink can be configured as a Virtual Chassis port.
